statement: Confirmed arc-05's mem-arc-05-0001 prediction: RR-6.1 (no-naked-domain-strings) fired on enforcer-lang-rust's own private Finding-builder helpers (push(&mut self, line: u32, marker: &str), manifest_dir() -> PathBuf) in both no_reexports.rs and error_handling.rs — 4 findings, none are real domain-boundary violations (private, non-pub, no branded-newtype construction site). The RR-6.1 rule config still has no boundary-module allowlist as of this lane; the metric remains unfalsifiable exactly as L15 in orchestration-lessons.md describes.
why: Second independent lane (arc-05 then arc-06) hitting the identical false-positive-by-design pattern confirms this is systemic to every syn-AST validator crate that writes its own Finding-construction helpers, not a one-off. Spawned a background task (task_f2963010) rather than absorbing the fix into arc-06's scope, since the allowlist belongs to whichever pack owns the RR-6.1 rule config/params shape (a downstream RR-6 feature pack), not to arc-06's skeleton+baseline owns.
howToApply: Any future enforcer-lang-* crate author should expect ocentra_enforcer_check --check no-naked-domain-strings to fire on their own private helper functions that take &str/String/PathBuf; do not try to fix it by re-typing those signatures to branded newtypes (that would be over-engineering internal glue) — file/spawn a task against the RR-6.1 rule config instead, per L15's prescription (boundary-module glob allowlist).

evidence.ref: ocentra_enforcer_check no-naked-domain-strings on crates/enforcer-lang-rust/src/rules/{no_reexports,error_handling}.rs: 4 findings at no_reexports.rs:81,177 and error_handling.rs:91,204

statement: syn 2.x's Visit trait calls visit_macro(&Macro) for EVERY macro invocation regardless of syntactic position (expression, statement, or item context) — including macros that also arrive wrapped in an ExprMacro node. Overriding BOTH visit_expr_macro and visit_macro for the same banned-macro-name check double-counts any macro call that appears in expression position (e.g. dbg!(x) as a tail expression matched both nodes in local testing, inflating the finding count from 4 to 5 for 4 seeded macro calls).
why: This is the kind of syn::visit::Visit double-dispatch gotcha that silently produces wrong finding counts (not a compile error, not an obviously-wrong single-fixture test) — it only surfaced because the fixture had exactly one macro call in expression-tail position among four, and the parity harness's exact-count style test caught the off-by-one.
howToApply: When writing a syn::visit::Visit-based Validator that bans specific macro names, implement the check ONCE in visit_macro (the single point syn calls for every macro invocation) and do NOT also override visit_expr_macro/visit_stmt_macro for the same check — those nodes wrap the same Macro syn already routes through visit_macro, so a second override double-counts expression/statement-position calls.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-lang-rust/src/rules/error_handling.rs — panic_todo_unimplemented_dbg_all_fire_in_first_party_code test failed left=5 right=4 before removing the redundant visit_expr_macro override
